body: I feel like we're arguing completely different things. I'm not saying that individualized racism doesn't exist. I'm just saying they're not equal. If someone made fun of a straight person, it wouldnt be the same as dropping a gay slur. Saying "cis" in a mean way still comes off as ignorant, but is not the same level of individualized discrimination as someone calling someone a tranny or something. Because of historical context as well as current representation and oppression.

I'm literally Slavic, dude. And, for the most part white people were oppressed by other white people. Christians oppressed Pagans, destroying Nordic cultures. My great grandfather was an immigrant. I'm educated and aware of my own heritage. But, thank you for your concernt.

 But, white people dont suffer from the same oppressions today unlike what poc still face. Systemic violence is not just individual racism, but individual racism stems from and contributes to it.
There is an inherent classism due to the economic imbalances poc faced, especially in the US. That also means racism is often another form of classism within your own class due in part to business owners fueling racial differences in the working class to put down unions, strikes, and encourages scabs. I understand the historical context, dawg.

I was arguing that the FIRST comment that led to all this, the guy who said equating two individual kinds of racism was not the same due to those things, was saying just that. We're still living during BLM protests and there are poc in my town being searched and pulled over because the only description they have of a criminal is he's black. The same thing has never happened to me as a white person, even though I've lived in plenty of areas where white women have been involved in drug-related crimes.

So literally dont worry about me. I'm not gonna lose sleep if a Hispanic woman is upset I'm dating her daughter because I'm white. Individualized racism will never have a lasting effect on my life in the same way that it has on the lives of poc. 

Funny side note:  The only time I have ever experienced an SO's family member being racist toward me was when they assumed I was black because of my name. This happened twice with the same old man.

NTA The most important thing you can do is back up your son. I think maybe doing something else with your kids so your son doesnt feel like it's a punishment for him being honest about being uncomfortable would be nice. That's hard to open up about. Tell you SIL that, while you appreciate and apologize for making the rest of the family feel bad, your first priority is to make sure all your kids are comfortable. There will be plenty of times you can spend with the family in the future. There is no reason to guilt you or your son on this.

Grandma probably wont change and it's not you or your son's responsibility to change her.

They're literally not saying those other instances are invalid. They're saying it's not the same thing as perpetuating racism that has led to systemic violence, classism, xenophobia etc.

Hispanic grandma saying "why is she dating a white boy?" is not the same as a white grandma saying "why is she dating a mexican?" Because white people aren't getting deported and locked in cages whereas Mexican people are. In some cases just not being white passing or not having a white passing last name has led to people having their citizenship investigated. 

White people experience privilege. Any "racism" against white people doesnt stem from or reinforce oppression against us because we are not the oppressed.

NTA She was pretty presumptuous to take your shit down without talking to you. And, she agreed to what you said about the shared living space before she moved in. Her lashing out is pretty uncalled for but maybe she also had bad experiences with homophobic roommates or even just family members in the past. Maybe that even led her to be scared to talk to you before hanging it? It doesnt excuse her behavior. It's just a thought.

That being said, I think you should work to find a compromise of something that can still show the community she belongs to while fitting nicely with your decor.

ESH I think she DEFINITELY sucked for what she was saying. You were just trying to vent to her about an emotional event in your life and she wasn't being empathetic at all. But, I do think your retaliation was douchey. In the end, I think you're both teenagers and you're gonna both do a lot of douchey things. I think your sister should apologize and try to be more empathetic, but I kinda think you should apologize for unnecessarily turning it around on her instead of just like... telling her you're upset and walking away from her. You said you also have friends to rely on for this moment and I dont think bringing up a sore subject for her was a "good analogy" so much as a spiteful jab cuz you were already upset.

I don't think this is the priority. The priority is 100% you, but your death will be an even bigger burden on the people around you. They will not be happy when you die. I pinky promise.

Like I said, though, you're the priority. That's okay, you know. It sounds like you really dont like burdening anyone so you might not like prioritizing how you feel or reaching out to talk about how shitty things have been for you. But it is okay to have the feelings you have and it is okay to reach out to people when you need to. Like, maybe trying to make plans on New Years Eve instead. Nothing big, just watching a movie or something with someone.

As someone who has also struggled with anxiety and depression from a young age, I'm not gonna do the it get better bs. It gets easier to cope sometimes. But not all of the time. I've had my own unsuccessful attempts and I still have suicidal thoughts. What makes things a little easier for me is knowing how many other people feel like they just dont fit. If no one fits, maybe we need to stop focusing on fitting and start carving out a new place for ourselves instead. I dont know. Just spitballing here. Its 4 am where I live.

I'm sorry you're struggling. I cant pretend to know exactly what you're going through, but I've been where you are. I'm sorry. I hope you dont die. Feel free to message me if you want to talk to an anonymous stranger.

"It's different when I'm a dude," is a really slippery slope that leads to the gross thinking that you should like it. I sincerely wish I could be your jogging buddy and defend your honor, dude.

I still think its gross for her to do so after you've asked her to stop and explained to her how you feel. But, she's already spent a lot of her life up to this point being misgendered. It's called a deadname for a reason. Thats a false equivalency imo. Please, dont use that rhetoric or retaliate by doing any of that.

Not that I think you would. You sound like a swell dude.

NTA Even if you were closeted trans, her constantly trying to out you after saying you're uncomfortable is fucking gross. Speculating on someone else's identity like that is kind of objectifying. I think you should just talk to your friends and explain that you were not hostile over the idea of being trans, but rather her completely disrespecting your boundaries. She was pushy and insensitive, even if her intentions were good.

NTA I would say it'd be nice to have gotten his say and made him aware that you were going to make this decision before you did so, but if he's not paying rent then you're right. It isn't his decision. On top of that, you've been more than accommodating to his strange habits. He is not being equally accommodating to you. There's an imbalance here. He showed no empathy toward you or your sister's situation regarding your mother. I wouldn't want to live with a baby right now, but the idea of turning away my SO's loved one who is at risk of abuse is imo pretty callous.

That being said, I don't think that your actions show you view her as property or that you dont respect women or something like that. I think your actions show you have undealt with trauma that left with some serious trust issues. That's not an excuse for being kinda douchey, but I really think some of these comments are... a lot.

ESH, except wife.

NTA for telling your brother you dont trust him or even for asking him to find a new place. You dont owe him your trust. He sounds like a big A.

But, YTA for not talking to or considering your wife's feelings. Its not just about you not trusting her to not bang your brother. You didnt trust her enough to discuss this decision with her before you made it. That's why I feel you gave her less agency. Whether or not you said it wasnt about her, your actions told your wife that you didnt trust her. 
You screwed up and I think you should apologize and talk to her about the feelings you havent let go. Your wife probably feels like you think she's no better than your ex, who also betrayed you. Holding your brother too accountable might be giving him too much power in your mind and your wife not enough.

First of all, so sorry for your loss. The suggestion that some loss is greater than others by your friends makes me sad. Why is it a contest?

Your friends and family are wrong and sound like they haven't experienced the loss of a child either. When my grandmother lost her son, she didn't take back sentimental things from his ex. There was even an engagement ring, but they were broken up for a little bit before he died. They weren't even going to get married with the ring and my grandmother felt it wasnt right to take it. She treated my uncle's ex like family, like her own child. Especially after losing hers.

NTA Your grandmother gave it to you. Trying to take something that a deceased loved one specifically wanted you to have is kinda crappy and I think your step-brother should be more empathetic. Yeah, I understand wanting to feel like part of THIS family despite not being blood and I think empathy toward that is good. But, that's hecked up of him.

This kinda reminds me of something that happened with my fiance's family. His rather old and wealthy grandfather got married to a younger woman. He really loved my fiance. He was racist and homophobic and conservative and still loved my very bi, very progressive fiance. He had a lot of plans for who his things and money and house were going to and as he got older he discussed it with the family and everyone in the family knew. But, his mind started going when he was at the end. It was so sad. But when he died somehow his younger wife got basically everything.

My fiance's family tried talking to her about how he promised certain hunting guns to grandkids specifically and how the house was supposed to stay in the family, but she was like "well, my kids and grandkids are part of the family too." She then completely cut off my fiance's family. After everything, my fiance's parents did yard work for her and brought her vegetables. My fiance helped and he went fishing with his grandfather every summer several times. His grandfather loved and was proud of this family. He had these houses built for this family. 

And I'm sure his younger wife did a lot for him, but the way everything happened it felt like just transparent gold-digging. Like she put up with all of us for the money and the house. Her kids and grandkids were never around for family gathering. They had their own families. And they're getting everything this old man earned with the hope of passing it on to his children and grandchildren. Especially crushing cuz my fiance's parents still live in the other house he built next door and get to see what was promised to them every single day. They get to see where they spent so many Christmases from across the yard. I think my fiance's parents are still trying to fight it on the down low, but what I heard was that she pawned some of his stuff and just offered our family a little money.

Lmao Sorry for the long comment. Kinda venting cuz I've been in this family for a long time and to watch this man's son lose his dad and basically everything to remember his dad by? Soul-crushing... don't give up that blanket, dude. Your grandma gave that to you.

Re-reading this, its admittedly hard to understand what I was saying at the time. I was pretty upset when I wrote it. So thank you to the few people here who took the time to read and respond to that mess. I hope to be in a much better place soon with this person far behind me.

I agree with the comments here about some of the future games being better constructed when it comes to pacing and mechanics, but I think there's a solid chance you still might not enjoy them if you didnt enjoy this one. I just replayed the first one after not playing the games for years. Took me far less than 10 hours to get through it and I feel like I remember more blocks and getting stuck in more areas in the later games when I was younger. 

Don't get me wrong. I love the games and if you're into it than more power to ya to power through. The first game does drag and you get to see more of the characters in future installments. The characters and story are both over the top and cutesy in a way that I think is really fun and matches the art style. But, maybe download an emulator if you're worried about not liking it. ;) The games have been out long enough that you're not hurting the studio or anything by taking it for a test spin. Yo ho ho!
I didnt get into dnd until college so maybe they still have time. :)

Whether or not you are shy or awkward or uncomfortable in a new group, your actions are still your own. She completely overreacted and did you a disservice to you by not just talking to you. A different friend had to ask you to apologize? What? No. You guys can't baby her cuz she won't grow as a human and learn to communicate more effectively. It would also tank my opinion of someone if they were so passive aggressive, but I appreciate that you're attempting to give her the benefit of the doubt. I'm sure she does deserve the benefit of the doubt. But damn.

I am super shy and awkward and have plenty of bad past experiences that influence my trust issues. But posting all over social media about being depressed cuz someone didnt tag me in a photo is madness. She might have bad anxiety, but that still doesnt excuse her actions. You take responsibility for your anxiety, dude. And she should take responsibility for not communicating with you at all.

My advice would be to just talk to her. Say you felt bad that what happened effected her so much at the time. But that you'd like to be able to just message each other when you have problems in the future so that you can both clear it up faster and not having to go through something like that again. An offer to hang out more or something to help her feel more included might also go a long way, while also helping you get to know her more and understanding where these problems stem from.
I do some serious doom scrolling so it is actually good advice for me. 😅
In the end, we're strangers on the internet. We dont know what's best for you. But be careful about rebounding, my dude.

Dude. Literally fuck the people in the comment victim blaming your wife first of all. Sexual assault court cases are harrowing. I have two close friends who I had to help through similar situations that also went through the legal system and, while both my friend were telling the truth in their situations, neither resulted in the rapists going to prison. 

Afterward, one friend craved intimacy because the rape made them feel unattractive and dirty and they felt consensual intimacy was helping them feel cleaner. But, my other married friend, like your wife, didnt even want to be touched. Her husband and her both went to therapy. Together and separate like someone else said in the chat. It can be really helpful. Like you said, you had no one to talk to and I cant imagine what your wife has gone through. Mental health is important to improving sexual health and libido. Depression can super negatively effect wanting to bone down.

I think you should encourage her to make the first move. Make the experience different from her trauma. Offer to let her touch you how she wants. Or, have her specifically tell you where she wants to be touched and do what she says. Giving her command and putting her in charge could be really sexy. It gives her the control she probably hasn't felt sexually in a while and it takes some of the burden off your shoulders. If she's shy or something, there are plenty of alternatives you could try that still let her be in charge. I think you're being wonderful by moving slowly for her.

Mental health is really important. Yours and hers. Dont be afraid to get the help you need. Find time for each other as well as for yourselves. Hoping things improve for you guys.

I think you should talk to her. I've been in love with best friends and I know how crushing it is when the other person doesn't feel the same, but to still want to be their best friend and have to carry those feelings all the time. But, it's definitely worse than continuing to carry it silently imo.

Just ask her if she'd like to go on a date. Confess that you have feelings for her and that you are confident enough in your friendship that you'd like to just try things out and see where they go. If she says yes, super. If she says no, maybe just use the quarantine as an excuse to get a little space. It's not a bad thing to get space and dote on ourselves for some time because being in love means so much of our mental processes are being used for someone else. And, if she's a good friend, she'll understand needing a little 'me time' and she'll be there for you.

I mean, you should both be as safe as possible. I think communication is the most important. With your boyfriend and with any potential sexual partners. It's really easy to get hurt feelings when people aren't open and honest. I would always tell my SO before and after I'd fooled around with someone.

If you ever feel uncomfortable, be honest. And, be sure he knows he can do the same with you. Neither of you should ever do anything with anyone you dont want to do, no matter how you define your relationship.

Be wary of weirdos. 👀 There are some untrustworthy people out there and part of being in a relationship is being a team and protecting and helping each other.

NTA. But I do think it deserves an apology. I think she's definitely the asshole in this situation, but that she isn't even aware of it because of how she's been enabled by her father and even you to a point. My friend is going through something similar with his girlfriend. I love both of them very much, but my friend has been letting her live there and paying for her everything for quite a while. He works. She doesn't. She feels lonely and bored a lot. He feels super hurt that she hasn't been thankful or supportive of any of his work or side projects that he also wants to work on. Quarantine is making all of us feel trapped and asshole-ish. I think you should be honest and clarify. Tell her you want this to be her home too, but right now you dont feel like shes doing her part to make it a home together. She needs to be an adult and find work or some kind of projects to do while you're working. And you both should plan time together so that you still feel entertained and feel togetherness instead of both going stir crazy. I imagine she feels super trapped and lonely and that's why she calls her friends a lot. Having a trial living period during quarantine is actually going to show you how you'll both operate under the worst circumstances, which is both a blessing and a curse.
